mesh.empty: game drew a mesh with no meshes in the catalog

material.empty: game used a material with no materials in the catalog

sound.doc: Sound clips, by the IDs the game plays them with.
sound.empty: game played a sound with no sounds in the catalog

max.doc: Counts travel in float32 lanes: the wire format's exact-integer range, not a runtime memory budget.

state.message: game state must be a bounded array of finite float32 values
state.schemaMessage: state schema must be an integer in 1..16777215

limits.doc: Reserved extension tag for optional development provenance; game section tags start at 1.
The most UTF-8 JSON bytes, each encoded as one float32 lane, in a frame's provenance.
The most source/object associations in one frame; no history is retained by the decoder.
The most UTF-8 bytes in a provenance object ID, system label or source filename.
Counts travel in float32 lanes: the wire format's exact-integer range, not a runtime memory budget.
Faces of one convex solid; games may use fewer.
The widest or tallest field.
The most extra vec4s one draw may carry.
The most nodes one frame's interface may have.
The most code points one interface node's name, description and value text may have together.
Interface node ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.
The most service requests one frame may make.
The most values (a text's code points, or a compute service's numbers) one service request or answer carries.
Service request ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.
Operation codes run from 0 to this; each service numbers its own.
The most voices one frame may declare.
The most buses one frame may declare, the master (bus 0) included.
Voice ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.

The time constant, in milliseconds, of the glide that takes a voice's or bus's gain, pan, pitch, lowpass and reverb toward a frame's new value (WebAudio's setTargetAtTime), so that values set every frame do not click.
The shortest fade, in milliseconds, of a voice that leaves or changes clip.
A lowpass cutoff, in Hz, at or above which a filter is open; hosts also leave one open at or above half their sample rate.
The most pose layers one frame may have.
The most particle emitters one frame may have.
The most particles one emitter has alive at once (its rate times its lifetime, rounded up); hosts leave out the rest.
The most of a game's own sections one frame may carry.
A game's own sections and events are numbered from 1 to this.
The most lanes one of a game's own sections may carry.
Gamepads connected at once that the game hears of: pads are numbered from 0 to one less than this.
Actions a game declares (the input service's declare): they are numbered from 0 to one less than this.
Bindings one action holds, its defaults and the player's alike.
Touches down at once that the game hears of: they are numbered from 0 to one less than this.
The most point and spot lights one frame may have.
Preference events from this index on carry the engine's preferences (ENGINE_PREFERENCE_*); below it, the game's own.
The most panners one frame may declare: one for each voice and sound it may have.

enumerations.name: TestDriverOp
enumerations.doc: Version-1 native session test commands. Available only to a separate test guest in pen test-blot --session.

enumerations.name: UiRole
enumerations.doc: What an interface node is; hosts expose it with the matching role. A textbox's value text is the text in it; a log is a list of messages whose newest lines a screen reader may announce.

enumerations.name: UiAction
enumerations.doc: What assistive technology, or the game's keyboard focus, does to an interface node: moves the focus to it or away from it, does what clicking it does, steps its value up or down or sets it (to the UiAction event's value), opens or closes it. A node lists the actions it takes in its `actions` bits, 1 << code each.

enumerations.name: UiState
enumerations.doc: An interface node's checked, expanded or selected state: none for a node without one.

enumerations.name: UiLive
enumerations.doc: Whether assistive technology announces an interface node's changes as they come, and how urgently.

enumerations.name: Service
enumerations.doc: Which service a request is for: Steam's achievements, stats and rich presence, the system clipboard, the browser for a web address, what the game runs on, a native compute library (grid pathfinding), the host's developer tools (DEVTOOLS_OP_*), which only a dev tools program asks of, the simulation services both hosts answer alike, bit for bit: rigid-body physics, paths over a navmesh, ray and shape queries against colliders, and noise and heightfields, the game's actions and their bindings (INPUT_OP_*), the engine's preferences (PREFERENCES_OP_*), the player's language (LOCALE_OP_*), the captions of the sounds that play (CAPTIONS_OP_*) and the player's consent to crash and performance reports (REPORTS_OP_*). A host without one answers unavailable.

enumerations.name: ServiceStatus
enumerations.doc: How a service request went: done; the service is not there (Steam is off, no clipboard, the browser cannot); it is there but refused or failed; or the host does not know the service or operation.

enumerations.name: SteamOperation
enumerations.doc: Steam's operations. Achievements and stats go by their API names (the text); set_stat and set_stat_float set `a`, add_stat adds `a` to an integer stat, and these and get_stat answer the stat's value. set_presence sets rich presence key (the text's first `a` code points) to the rest of the text; clear_presence clears every key. status answers ok while Steam runs for the game, unavailable otherwise. Steam Input: input_action_set activates the action set named by the text on every controller, input_glyph answers the path of the glyph image of the first button or stick bound to the action named by the text in the active set (a digital action, or an analog one), and input_panel opens Steam's binding panel, where the player rebinds them; each answers unavailable without Steam Input or a controller. The Workshop's: workshop_publish uploads the player's saved scene (the editor's) as an item titled with the text, visible to `a` (0 everyone, 1 friends, 2 only the player, 3 those with the link), or with `b` 1 as a new version of the item whose id is the text's first line, answered later with the item's id as text and value 1 when the player must accept the Workshop's agreement; workshop_items answers the installed subscribed items' ids as text, a space between them, their count the value, and downloads the rest; workshop_subscribe and workshop_unsubscribe take an item's id as text and answer once Steam has; workshop_use makes an installed item's scene the player's, for the game to load as the editor's scene.

enumerations.name: ClipboardOperation
enumerations.doc: The clipboard's operations: copy the text to it, or answer with the text on it.

enumerations.name: UrlOperation
enumerations.doc: Open the http or https address in the text in the player's browser.

enumerations.name: PlatformOperation
enumerations.doc: What the game runs on, answered as text: the operating system (linux, windows, macos, web), the player's locale (a BCP 47 tag, en-US), and the device (value 1 on a Steam Deck, with its name as text).

enumerations.name: PathfindingOperation
enumerations.doc: The shortest 4-connected path over a grid of `a` columns and `b` rows whose cells are the request's values (0 open, anything else blocked), from cell `c` to cell `d` (row * columns + column): it answers the path's cells in order, start and goal included, its length as the value, or none when there is no path.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsOperation
enumerations.doc: The host's developer tools. log answers the log's lines from serial `a` on, value the serial after the last, each line as its source (0 game, 1 build, 2 reload, 3 asset, 4 pipeline, 5 session), 1 if an error, its length and its code points. frame answers the last frame's numbers in DEVTOOLS_FRAME's order, timing the game's frames while `a` is 1. gpu answers the graphics adapter's name. command sends the game console command `a` with argument `b`. pause and play stop and start the game's clock; step runs `a` frames and stays paused; rewind goes back `a` seconds of game time, paused; replay plays the last `a` seconds again, then live; history keeps the past to travel in (unavailable answers what needs it while none is kept). record starts recording the input to the text's path, or a new file when it is empty, or stops a recording. shot saves the window with the dev tools over it to the text's path, or a new file. tune sets the live-tunable constant whose id is `a` to `b`, and tuned answers the game's tuned values as id and value pairs. bake writes them into the checkout as the defaults, or only the one whose id is `a` when `a` is not 0. packets keeps each frame's input and render packets from now on while `a` is 1 (the last 120 frames), or forgets them at 0, and answers the frames kept, oldest first, each as DEVTOOLS_PACKET's numbers; packet_diff answers how frame `b` differs from frame `a`, both kept: for each of DEVTOOLS_PACKET's numbers after position, its count in `a`, its count in `b` and how many of its elements differ. state answers the live state's sections (`a` below 0), each its key, version, width and length, value the state's schema, or up to 256 lanes of section `a` from lane `b` on, value its length; with `c` above 0, of the state the history kept `c` seconds of game time back instead. state_diff answers, for each section of the live state or the one kept `a` seconds back, its key, its length then and now, how many lanes differ and the first that does (-1 for none), value the frame compared with. pictures takes a picture of the game's frame each time the history could keep a moment, while `a` is 1, into the dev tools' atlas (the texture of material `b`: slots of 128 by 80 pixels, 8 to a row, the first 16 for pictures), and answers each picture's slot and the frame that shows it, oldest first; seek goes to frame `a`, paused. watch pauses the game once lane `b` of the live state's section `a` compares with `d` as DEVTOOLS_COMPARE `c` says, `a` -1 stops watching and -2 only asks; it answers the watch: key, lane, comparison, value, the lane's value now and the frame it paused at (-1 for none). profile samples the game's guest while `a` is 1, stops at 0 and forgets the samples at 2 (3 only asks), answering how many it has and 1 while sampling; flame answers them as a flame graph, value the samples: first how many functions follow that the samples found running most, each its function index, samples, its name's length and code points; then each node (a caller before its callees) as its depth, function index, first sample, samples, samples in it alone, its name's length and code points. memory answers the game's committed memory in bytes, the most it committed, then for each counter the guest exports (guest ABI 3's ownership counters) and the host's calls into it, its name's length, code points and value in two 24-bit halves, value the number of counters. presets answers the names of the checkout's tunable presets, a line each; preset_save saves the game's tuned values as the preset the text names, and preset_load tunes each value of that preset. assets answers the game's catalog of DEVTOOLS_ASSET `a`, each entry as its DEVTOOLS_ASSET_STATE, its revision, its key's length and code points. preview draws catalog asset `b` of kind `a` (a mesh with material `c`, a material on mesh `c`) into slot `d` (16 to 63) of the atlas pictures named, value 1 once drawn and 0 while its assets load. swap draws catalog asset `b` of kind `a` from the asset the text names instead, or its own again when the text is empty, until the next build. material answers material `a`'s color and instance parameters (8 numbers, 0 when it sets none), whether it sets them (two numbers), then its shader's and texture's names, each its length and code points; material_set sets number `b` of those 8 in the checkout's file to `c`, which then reloads. audit checks the game's interface as the last frame showed it and answers its findings: value their count, and for each its kind (AUDIT_FINDING_*), the node's id, a measure (a contrast ratio, a size in pixels, or 0), its message's length and the message's code points. audio answers the mix as it plays: DEVTOOLS_AUDIO's numbers, then DEVTOOLS_BUS's for each bus, the master first; peaks and RMS are linear and over what played since the last audio answer. mute silences bus `a` while `b` is 1 and solo hears only the soloed buses (and the master's own voices) while any is soloed; both are the developer's, never the game's or a recording's. export hands the game's state over as a save file named by the text, or a new one (the browser downloads it); import loads a save file the player hands over (the browser asks for one), or plays an input recording. systems measures named game systems while a is 1, stops at 0, and answers a bounded page starting at row b (64 rows maximum). Row zero refreshes the snapshot; subsequent pages read that same snapshot. Value is the total system count. Each row contains stage (Start through Settle, 0-6), id, calls since the previous snapshot, mean milliseconds, maximum milliseconds, execution mode (0 sequential), mean requested allocation bytes per call, mean allocation count per call, name length and code points. Uncalled systems have -1 timings; allocation means are -1 without allocation instrumentation or calls. Unsupported hosts answer unavailable. semantic exchanges bounded JSON text for opt-in application descriptors, decoded object values, decision events, watches and exact timeline seeks; see docs/semantic-inspection.md for version 1, limits, pagination and explicit unavailable reasons.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsFrame
enumerations.doc: Where each number sits in a devtools frame answer: the milliseconds since the frame before; the game's frame phases in milliseconds (guest, waited for an overlapped guest, packet decode, validation, rendering, surface acquisition, presentation, explicit pacing waits, housekeeping, and their total), each -1 when the frame was not timed or did not run. Drawing phases do not overlap: render covers preparation, uploads, command encoding, queue submission and the developer overlay, excluding acquire and present calls; acquire and present include any waits inside those calls. Pace covers browser GPU backpressure and repaint waits (zero natively, whose event-loop pacing is outside the measured frame). These are wall-clock call durations, not thread CPU time; driver stalls inside queue submission remain in render. Housekeeping includes audio, input and capture work. Then its packet's bytes; the renderer's draw calls, instanced ones and instances; the frame's meshes and brushes; the game's memory in bytes; the frame's width and height in pixels; and the timeline: the next frame's position, 1 when paused, replaying, keeping history or overlapping frames, and the frame an input recording started at, or -1. Then the renderer's culling: draws and instances left out of the camera's view, and casters left out of the shadow maps (once for each map); the triangles drawn; the render scale the scene drew at; and the GPU's milliseconds over a recent frame's shadow maps, culling, scene, the passes after it, sprites and insets, and the whole frame, each -1 where the GPU has no timestamps.

enumerations.name: PhysicsOperation
enumerations.doc: Rigid-body physics (rapier), from the world the request sends: step advances it `a` steps (1 to 600) of `b` seconds (up to 1) with gravity `c` (metres per second squared along y). The values are its bodies, each a kind (PHYSICS_BODY_*), a collider (COLLIDER_SHAPE_*'s record: shape, size x y z, position x y z, rotation quaternion x y z w), linear velocity x y z, angular velocity x y z (radians a second), friction, restitution and density, then its shape's data. The answer's values are each body's position x y z, rotation x y z w, linear and angular velocity, 13 values in the request's order, then the contacts touching after the last step, 9 values each: the two bodies' indices (the lower first), the deepest point x y z, the normal x y z from the first to the second, and their distance (negative while they overlap); its value is the contacts' count. The world is the request's alone: nothing carries over to the next.

enumerations.name: PhysicsBody
enumerations.doc: How a physics body moves: never; under gravity and contacts; or by its velocity alone, pushing what it meets.

enumerations.name: ColliderShape
enumerations.doc: A collider's shape, and what its size and data mean: a ball of radius x; a cuboid of half extents x y z; a capsule and a cylinder of radius x and half height y along their y axis; the convex hull of x points, its data x y z each; a heightfield of x columns by y rows of samples z metres apart, centred on its position, its data the heights row by row from -z, each row from -x; and a triangle mesh of x vertices and y triangles, its data the vertices x y z, then each triangle's three vertex indices. Coordinates, sizes, heights and speeds lie within a million metres (a second): a request past that fails.

enumerations.name: NavmeshOperation
enumerations.doc: Paths over a navmesh on the ground plane (x, z), triangulated from areas. The values are an agent's radius, then areas: each a kind (NAVMESH_AREA_*), a corner count and the corners' x z. The ground is walkable where a walkable area covers it and no obstacle does. find answers a short way from (`a`, `b`) to (`c`, `d`), its turns kept the radius off the corners they round and crossing no navmesh edge narrower than twice it, as x z points from start to goal, value their count; a start or goal off the navmesh moves to its nearest point, and none answers when the goal cannot be reached. triangles answers the walkable triangles, x z of each corner, value their count.

enumerations.name: NavmeshArea
enumerations.doc: What a navmesh area is: ground to walk on, or something in the way.

enumerations.name: SpatialOperation
enumerations.doc: Queries against `a` colliders, the request's first values (COLLIDER_SHAPE_*'s records with their data). raycast casts the rays that follow (origin x y z, direction x y z) up to `b` metres, a ray starting inside a shape hitting it at once while `c` is 1, and answers for each the collider it hits first (its index + 1, 0 for none), the distance and the surface's normal x y z, value the hits' count. overlap answers the indices of the colliders a query collider (the record that follows) touches, in order, value their count. nearest answers for each point that follows (x y z) the nearest collider within `b` metres (index + 1, 0 for none), the distance (0 inside) and its closest point x y z, value how many found one.

enumerations.name: NoiseOperation
enumerations.doc: Deterministic simplex noise summed in octaves, the same on every host. The values start with its frequency (cycles a metre), amplitude, lacunarity (each octave's frequency over the last's), gain (each octave's amplitude over the last's) and style (NOISE_STYLE_*); `c` is the seed and `d` the octaves (1 to 16). heightfield answers a grid of `a` columns by `b` rows of heights, row by row, from the corner x z the next two values give, the last its spacing in metres (its rows along +z, its columns along +x). sample answers the height at each x z pair that follows. Heights stay within the amplitude; the value is their count.

enumerations.name: NoiseStyle
enumerations.doc: How noise octaves add up: fractal Brownian motion (rolling hills), or ridged (sharp crests where the noise crosses zero).

enumerations.name: GamepadButton
enumerations.doc: A gamepad's buttons, in the order of the browser's standard gamepad: the four face buttons by where they sit (south is Xbox's A, PlayStation's cross), the shoulder buttons, the triggers (analog: their GamepadButton value runs from 0 to 1), select and start, the sticks pressed in, the directional pad and the home button.

enumerations.name: GamepadAxis
enumerations.doc: A gamepad's stick axes, in the order of the browser's standard gamepad: from -1 to 1, right and down positive.

enumerations.name: InputDevice
enumerations.doc: What moved an action (the Action event's device): the keyboard or mouse, a gamepad, Steam Input, or a touch screen. A game shows the prompts of the device the player used last.

enumerations.name: InputSource
enumerations.doc: What a binding reads: a key (its code, as KeyDown events carry it), a mouse button (numbered as PointerDown events number them), a gamepad button (GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*) or a gamepad axis (GAMEPAD_AXIS_*). A binding is three numbers: its source, its code and its scale, which multiplies what it reads (a key or button reads 1 held, an axis -1 to 1), so -1 makes a key push an axis action the other way and an axis bound with -1 reads its other half.

enumerations.name: InputOperation
enumerations.doc: The input service's operations, on action `a` (0 to MAX_ACTIONS - 1). declare declares it: `b` is 0 for a button (its value 1 while a binding holds it at half or more, else 0) or 1 for an axis (its value the bindings' sum, from -1 to 1), its values its name's `c` code points and then its default bindings, three numbers each (INPUT_SOURCE_*); it answers how many bindings it has, the player's if they rebound it. capture binds slot `b` to the next key, mouse button, gamepad button or stick the player presses (Escape gives up, answered failed), answering the binding as its values when it comes; cancel gives a capture up. bind sets slot `b` to the binding in the values, unbind removes slot `b`, reset gives the action its defaults back (every action's when `a` is MAX_ACTIONS), and bindings answers its bindings. The host keeps the player's bindings with their preferences.

enumerations.name: TouchPhase
enumerations.doc: Where a touch is (the Touch event's phase): put down, moved, lifted, or taken away by the system (a gesture it claimed, the window losing the focus).

enumerations.name: DevtoolsPacket
enumerations.doc: Where each number sits in a devtools packets answer's frame: its position; its input's events and lanes; its render packet's lanes; its settings (camera, light, sky, quality and the rest, one element whose fields a diff counts); its draws, solids, decals, sounds, sprites, insets, field patches, interface nodes, service requests, buses and voices; and its requests to save, load, save and load the scene, checkpoint, undo, redo and exit, a bit each from 1 up.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsCompare
enumerations.doc: How a devtools watch compares a lane of the game's state with its value: equal to it, not equal, below it, above it, or (the value ignored) changed from what the lane held when the watch started.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsAsset
enumerations.doc: The kinds of the game's catalog a devtools assets, preview or swap request names.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsAssetState
enumerations.doc: Where a catalog asset stands in the host: not asked for yet, loading, ready to use, or failed to load (its last good revision, if any, still used).

enumerations.name: EnginePreference
enumerations.doc: The engine's own preferences, the same for every game: the player sets them through the host (its options, the platform's settings) or a game's settings (the preferences service), and the host keeps them. color_filter is a COLOR_FILTER_* the renderer applies to the whole picture, filter_strength how much of it (0 to 1), text_scale how much larger the game draws its text (1 to 2) and reduced_motion 1 when the player wants as little motion as can be (camera flights, shakes, slides and flashes left out). They reach the game as Preference events at index ENGINE_PREFERENCES plus the preference, played back as the game's own are.

enumerations.name: ColorFilter
enumerations.doc: A colour filter for colour vision deficiency: none, or the colours shifted so that those a player without red (protanopia), green (deuteranopia) or blue (tritanopia) cones confuses tell apart again; achromatopsia shows the picture in greys of its luminance.

enumerations.name: PreferencesOperation
enumerations.doc: The engine's preferences (ENGINE_PREFERENCE_*): set stores preference `a` as `b`, which the host applies at once and plays back to the game from then on, and answers the value it kept (clamped to the preference's range), or failed for a preference or value it does not take.

enumerations.name: LocaleOperation
enumerations.doc: The player's language, from the game's string tables (its text.json, and locales/TAG.json for each language). text answers the string whose key is the request's text in the player's language, laid out to draw left to right (right-to-left scripts reordered and Arabic joined), with `a` as its count when `b` is 1 (choosing the plural form and filling {count}); value 1 when it reads right to left, unavailable when no table has the key; where the text drawn differs from the text read (right to left), its values are the text drawn, a 0, then the text in reading order, unshaped, for assistive technology. language answers the language in use as a BCP 47 tag, value 1 for a right-to-left one. plural answers the plural category (PLURAL_CATEGORY_*) of count `a` in it as its value.

enumerations.name: PluralCategory
enumerations.doc: The plural categories of Unicode's CLDR, which choose a string's form for a count.

enumerations.name: AuditFinding
enumerations.doc: What an accessibility audit found: a node assistive technology cannot name (a control or an image without a name), a focus problem (a trap: a modal dialog with nothing to focus, or the keyboard unable to leave; a focus on a node the tree leaves out; two focused nodes), text whose contrast with what lies behind it is below WCAG's 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), or a control smaller than 24 by 24 pixels.

enumerations.name: CaptionsOperation
enumerations.doc: The captions the game's sounds carry (the assets' captions.json, by sound): text answers the caption of clip `a` as text, its value the seconds it shows for, or unavailable when the clip has none; active answers the captions showing now, newest first, one a line, its value how many.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsAudio
enumerations.doc: Where each number sits at the start of a devtools audio answer: the output's latency in milliseconds, from a frame's sound reaching the mixer to it leaving the speakers (-1 when the host cannot tell); the sample rate; the device's buffer, in samples a callback, as asked for or as the system chose (-1 while unknown); the voices and sounds playing, and those of them streamed; how often a stream ran dry so far; and how many buses follow.

enumerations.name: DevtoolsBus
enumerations.doc: Each bus's numbers in a devtools audio answer: its output's peak and RMS on the left and right since the last answer, and its state: 1 when a frame uses it, plus 2 when muted, plus 4 when soloed.

enumerations.name: DistanceModel
enumerations.doc: How a panner's gain falls with distance, as WebAudio's PannerNode distanceModel: linear from 1 at ref_distance to 1 - rolloff at max_distance; inverse, ref_distance / (ref_distance + rolloff * (distance - ref_distance)); exponential, (distance / ref_distance) ^ -rolloff; nearer than ref_distance is 1.

enumerations.name: ReportsOperation
enumerations.doc: Crash and performance reports for the game's developer, which the player opts into: consent answers what the player agreed to as its value, 1 for crash reports plus 2 for performance reports (0 for neither, as before they are asked); set_consent sets it to `a`, the same sum; queued answers how many reports wait to be sent. Each answers unavailable where nothing could be sent (a package whose developer gave no address for reports, a checkout, the browser), so that the game offers no choice with nothing behind it.

input.doc: The host's frame: the seconds since the last one, the viewport, its events and the state.

messages.frame: invalid frame clock, viewport or event count
messages.nonfinite: frame contains a nonfinite float32 value

events.name: KeyDown
events.doc: A key by its browser `KeyboardEvent.key` name ("a", "A", "ArrowLeft", "Shift", ...); the game gets its code.

events.name: AssetChanged
events.doc: An asset finished loading, or failed to.

events.name: Console
events.doc: A console command for the game: which, and its argument.

events.name: Preference
events.doc: A stored preference, played back when the game starts.

events.name: Tune
events.doc: A live-tunable constant set from the host: which, and its value.

events.name: UiAction
events.doc: An action on a node of the interface the game declared (the render packet's `ui`), from assistive technology: the node's id, the action (UI_ACTION_*), and the value set_value sets.

events.name: ServiceAnswer
events.doc: The answer to a service request the game made (the render packet's `services`), once, in a later frame: the request's id, how it went (SERVICE_STATUS_*), a number, and how many values (a text's code points, or numbers) follow in the ServiceData events right after it.

events.name: ServiceData
events.doc: Three of an answer's values, in order, after its ServiceAnswer: the request's id, then the values; lanes past the answer's length are zero.

events.name: GamepadConnected
events.doc: A gamepad was connected: its number, and 1 if its buttons and axes are laid out as the standard gamepad (GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*, GAMEPAD_AXIS_*), 0 if they come in the device's own order.

events.name: GamepadDisconnected
events.doc: A gamepad went away: its held buttons and moved axes came back first.

events.name: GamepadButton
events.doc: A gamepad button (GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*) changed: the pad, its value from 0 to 1, and 1 while it is pressed (at half or more).

events.name: GamepadAxis
events.doc: A gamepad axis (GAMEPAD_AXIS_*) moved: the pad and its value from -1 to 1, past the stick's dead zone (inside it, 0).

events.name: Action
events.doc: An action the game declared (the input service) changed: which, its value (a button's 1 or 0, an axis from -1 to 1) and the device that moved it (INPUT_DEVICE_*).

events.name: TextInput
events.doc: A character of text, typed, composed or committed by an input method, one code point an event, in order; or with composing 1, one of the composition's characters after its Composition event.

events.name: Composition
events.doc: An input method's composition (the text being composed, before it is committed) changed: its length in code points, which follow as TextInput events with composing 1, and the caret's place in it. A length of 0 ends it.

events.name: MouseMotion
events.doc: How far the mouse moved while the pointer is locked, unaccelerated where the platform allows: the device's counts natively, CSS pixels in a browser.

events.name: Touch
events.doc: A touch on the screen, by number (from 0, reused once lifted), where it is in window pixels, and its phase (TOUCH_PHASE_*). The first touch down also moves and presses the pointer (button 0), for games that only take the pointer.

events.name: Pan
events.doc: Touches dragged together: how far their centre moved, in window pixels, and how many there are.

events.name: Pinch
events.doc: Two touches moved apart or together: their centre, in window pixels, and the factor their distance grew by since the last Pinch.

events.name: Player
events.doc: In a net session (pen's docs/netplay.md) the events after it, up to the next Player, are this player's, numbered from 0 up to the players the game declares; every frame lists each player in order, events or none. Outside one there are none, and every event is player 0's.

events.name: SessionStarted
events.doc: The host session started, once after creating the game or restoring its initial save and before live frames. restored is 1 when the initial save matched the game's state schema and was restored, otherwise 0. Reloads, loads, rewinds and replays do not send it; it is not recorded as input.

events.name: RendererReady
events.doc: Once during an opted-in loading presentation after its scene, assets, pipelines and texture fades are ready. Delivered as a normal event so game-owned loading presentations can finish deterministically.

events.name: Game
events.doc: One of the game's own events, which its pen.json `protocol` declares: its tag there, and up to three values. Hosts send them only to a game that declares them, whose generated pen/extensions.blot decodes them; pen's own bindings leave them out.

render.doc: The game's frame: what to draw and play, and what to do.

messages.header: game returned an invalid frame header or state schema
messages.count: game returned an invalid frame count or flag
messages.length: game returned a truncated, oversized or nonfinite frame

quality.doc: How the game wants this frame drawn: samples per pixel, FXAA, render scale, texture filtering, ambient occlusion, a sky, screen effects, bloom and temporal antialiasing.

sky.doc: The sky's colors and the way toward the sun or moon.

fog.doc: Mist beyond `radius` of the middle; density 0 for none.

shadow.doc: The shadow map's view; `texels` 0 for no shadows.

clouds.doc: Clouds over the scene: how much of the sky they cover, 0 for none, and how far the wind has carried them along x and z.

checkpoint_requested.doc: An edit finished: the host records the scene for undo.

exit_requested.doc: The game is over: the host stops it.

aberration.doc: How far red moves from green, in screen heights across and down, and blue as far the other way, on the surfaces whose material asks for it.

sky.night.doc: 1 at full night, when stars show.

shadow.texel.doc: A map texel's width in world units.

blur.doc: How far the picture smears toward the middle of the screen, as a share of the way there (0 to 0.5), as speed would.

hide_cursor.doc: The frame supplies its own cursor and asks the host to hide the system one.

quality.taa.doc: Temporal antialiasing: each frame's samples move within their pixels and blend with the frames before, followed through the camera's motion.

loading.doc: The frame sprites are an application loading screen: draw them above the startup veil even while scene pipelines compile. Scene assets continue loading underneath.

show_captions.doc: Show sound captions when the player has enabled them in the game's accessibility settings. Off by default; the game owns and saves the choice.

max.doc: Counts travel in float32 lanes: the wire format's exact-integer range, not a runtime memory budget.

parameters.message: draw parameters must contain zero or four lanes
parameters.doc: Optional four shader values, overriding the material's instance defaults.

max.doc: The most extra vec4s one draw may carry.

extra.doc: Up to 32 more vec4s, flattened, that the shader reads after the parameters; a draw with any is drawn alone.

sections.name: solids
sections.doc: Convex solids: the points behind every face plane (normal · p <= distance).

record.name: Solid
record.doc: A convex solid: the points behind every face plane (normal · p <= distance).

max.doc: Faces of one convex solid; games may use fewer.

messages.mismatch: game returned solid lanes that do not match

sections.name: decals
sections.doc: Decals: `material`'s texture laid onto the surfaces inside the box, the cube -1..1 under `transform`, along its y axis, where their material takes decals; `opacity` fades it.

record.name: Decal
record.doc: `material`'s texture laid onto the surfaces inside the box, the cube -1..1 under `transform`, along its y axis, where their material takes decals; `opacity` fades it.

sections.name: sounds
sections.doc: Sounds to play once, each on a bus: gain, pan, pitch, lowpass and reverb send, all worked out by the game.

record.name: Sound

bus.doc: The bus it plays through; one the frame lacks passes it on to the master as it is.

reverb.doc: How much of it goes to the shared reverb.

record.doc: A sound to play once on a bus at the gain, pan, pitch, lowpass cutoff and reverb send given, all worked out by the game.

record.name: Sprite
record.doc: A rectangle over the screen, in pixels from its top left, drawn by its material's sprite shader, which reads the four `parameters` as it likes.

record.name: Inset

ambient.doc: Its own light: ambient, the way its rays travel, and their color.

draws.over: game returned more inset draws than it counted
draws.under: game returned inset draws that do not match

pixel_size.doc: Block size in screen pixels, or zero for a smooth image.

after_sprites.doc: Composite after this many frame sprites; zero draws below all sprites.

record.doc: A small 3D view over the screen, in the rectangle at (x, y).

parameters.message: draw parameters must contain zero or four lanes
parameters.doc: Optional four shader values, overriding the material's instance defaults.

max.doc: The most extra vec4s one draw may carry.

extra.doc: Up to 32 more vec4s, flattened, that the shader reads after the parameters; a draw with any is drawn alone.

sections.name: preferences
sections.doc: The player's preferences to store, when they changed, as many as the game keeps; the host plays them back as Preference events when the game starts.

sections.name: fields
sections.doc: Patches of the values the host keeps for some materials.

record.name: FieldPatch
record.doc: A patch of a field: a `width` x `height` grid of values the host keeps for `material`, which every draw of it reads as a texture at binding 3 (red, half-float). The patch's `columns` x `rows` values land row by row at column `x`, row `z`; the rest of the field keeps what it had.

max.doc: The widest or tallest field.
The widest or tallest field.

messages.mismatch: game returned field lanes that do not match

sections.name: ui
sections.doc: The interface the game declares for assistive technology and keyboard focus, every frame, whole: its nodes, parents first.

max.doc: The most nodes one frame's interface may have.

record.name: UiNode
record.doc: A node of the interface: its id, the same from frame to frame, its parent, what it is, where it lies on the screen in pixels from its top left (empty for one that is not drawn), its states, a range's value and bounds, the actions it takes, and its text: its name, description and value text one after the other, in code points.

max.doc: Interface node ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.

id.doc: 1 to MAX_UI_ID, from the node's key, so it stays the same.

max.doc: The most nodes one frame's interface may have.

parent.doc: Its parent's place in the section plus one, or 0 at the top. Parents come first: hosts put a node whose parent does not come before it at the top.

focused.doc: It has the game's keyboard focus.

modal.doc: A dialog that keeps the focus while it is open.

value.doc: A slider's or spin button's value, in its range.

max.doc: The most code points one interface node's name, description and value text may have together.

rest.name: text
rest.doc: Its name's code points, then its description's, then its value text's.

messages.invalid: game returned an invalid interface node
messages.mismatch: game returned interface lanes that do not match

sections.name: services
sections.doc: The frame's requests to services, each in one packet only: hosts answer each once, with ServiceAnswer and ServiceData events in a later frame, and a replay, whose recorded input holds the answers, asks no service again.

max.doc: The most service requests one frame may make.

record.name: ServiceRequest
record.doc: A request to a service: its id, unique in the run and never in two packets, which its answer carries back; the service (SERVICE_*) and its operation; four numbers; and its values: text as code points (an API name, the text to copy, an address), or the numbers a compute service takes.

max.doc: Service request ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.
Operation codes run from 0 to this; each service numbers its own.
The most values (a text's code points, or a compute service's numbers) one service request or answer carries.

rest.name: values
rest.doc: Its text's code points, or its numbers.

messages.invalid: game returned an invalid service request
messages.mismatch: game returned service lanes that do not match

sections.name: buses
sections.doc: The mix's buses, every frame, whole: the master first. A frame without buses plays everything through an open master at gain 1, the reverb coming back at 1; a bus it lacks is open and dry at gain 1.

record.name: Bus

reverb.doc: How much of it goes to the shared reverb; on the master, how loud the reverb comes back.

record.doc: A bus: the voices and sounds on it mix through its lowpass and gain into the master, and `reverb` of that goes to the shared reverb, as do their own sends through its lowpass and gain. Bus 0 is the master: everything passes through it last, the reverb's return included.

max.doc: The most buses one frame may declare, the master (bus 0) included.

sections.name: voices
sections.doc: The voices the game keeps playing, every frame, whole: hosts start, fade out and glide them by id.

record.name: Voice

max.doc: Voice ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.

id.doc: 1 to MAX_VOICE_ID, the same from frame to frame while it plays.

bus.doc: The bus it plays through; one the frame lacks passes it on to the master as it is.

reverb.doc: How much of it goes to the shared reverb.

start.doc: Seconds into the clip it starts from, round a looping clip as often as need be.

fade_in.doc: Seconds it fades in over as it starts.

fade_out.doc: Seconds it fades out over once frames leave it out.

record.doc: A voice the game keeps playing, declared by every frame that has it, whole. Hosts start a new id from `start`, fading in over `fade_in`; fade out an id the frame leaves out over its `fade_out` (at least AUDIO_FADE_MS), and one that comes back while fading returns where it is (over its `fade_in`, at least AUDIO_FADE_MS); start one whose clip or bus changed afresh, the old fading out; and glide the values that change (AUDIO_GLIDE_MS). A voice that does not loop plays once and is then silent for as long as frames keep it.

max.doc: The most voices one frame may declare.

sections.name: poses
sections.doc: The layers of skinned draws' poses: each samples one of its draw's mesh's clips at a time, and a draw's layers blend by their weights. A draw is posed when it has layers, its mesh a skin and its material's shader a `vertex_skinned` entry point; the host works out its joints' matrices and draws it alone.

record.name: Pose

draw.doc: The draw it poses: its place in the frame's draws.

clip.doc: Which of the mesh's clips, in the order its file lists them; one the mesh lacks counts for nothing.

time.doc: Seconds into the clip, round it as often as need be.

weight.doc: How much it counts among its draw's layers: 0 or more.

record.doc: A layer of a skinned draw's pose: clip `clip` of the draw's mesh at `time` seconds, counting `weight` among the draw's layers.

max.doc: The most pose layers one frame may have.

sections.name: emitters
sections.doc: Particle emitters, which hosts simulate on the GPU from each emitter's own clock and seed: every particle's path follows from them, so a frame's particles depend on that frame's emitters alone.

record.name: Emitter

material.doc: Its texture (round soft dots without one) and color, which tint every particle.

transform.doc: Where particles are born, and how their velocity turns.

seed.doc: What its particles' randomness follows from.

time.doc: Seconds since it began: particles are born `rate` a second from 0 on, each the same whatever the frame rate.

duration.doc: Seconds it gives birth for; 0 for as long as frames keep it.

radius.doc: Particles are born anywhere in the ball of this radius round the emitter.

velocity.doc: Each particle's velocity at birth, in the emitter's space.

spread.doc: A random velocity up to this fast, in any direction, added to each at birth.

gravity.doc: Acceleration in world space, units a second a second.

drag.doc: How fast velocity fades, a share a second: 0 for none.

size_start.doc: Particles' width in world units at birth, changing evenly to `size_end` at death.

color_start.doc: Particles' color at birth, changing evenly to `color_end` at death; alpha fades them.

additive.doc: Particles add their light to what is behind them, rather than covering it.

record.doc: A particle emitter: `rate` particles a second, each living `lifetime` seconds, born in a ball round `transform`'s origin and flying from it under gravity and drag, sized and colored over their lives.

max.doc: The most particle emitters one frame may have.

sections.name: lights
sections.doc: Point and spot lights beside the sun. The renderer sorts them into clusters of the view, which the shaders of lit materials read (pen-render's lights.wgsl).

record.name: Light

radius.doc: How far it reaches: its light falls smoothly to nothing there.

direction.doc: The way a spot light shines, a unit vector; a point light's is ignored.

inner.doc: The cosine of the half-angle within which a spot light is at full strength.

outer.doc: The cosine of the half-angle of a spot light's cone, where its light ends; -1 for a point light, which shines all round.

record.doc: A point light, or a spot light shining along `direction` within a cone, lighting what lies within `radius` of `position`.

max.doc: The most point and spot lights one frame may have.

sections.name: listener
sections.doc: Where the panners are heard from, as WebAudio's AudioListener: none, the camera (`view`'s eye, facing where it looks, its up the view's), or one listener.

record.name: Listener

up.doc: Its up, which with `forward` tells left from right.

record.doc: A listener: where it is, the way it faces and its up, in world units.

sections.name: panners
sections.doc: Voices and sounds heard from somewhere in the world, as WebAudio's PannerNode (equal-power panning) places them relative to the listener; the rest play as they are.

record.name: Panner

max.doc: Voice ids are whole numbers from 1 to this, the wire's exact-integer range.

voice.doc: The voice it places, by id, or 0 for a sound.

sound.doc: With `voice` 0, the sound it places, by its place in the frame's `sounds`.

orientation.doc: The way its cone faces; zero for none, heard alike from every side.

distance_model.doc: How its gain falls with distance (DISTANCE_MODEL_*).

ref_distance.doc: Within it, distance does not quiet it.

max_distance.doc: Beyond it, the linear model quiets it no further.

cone_inner.doc: The angle, in degrees, of the cone it is heard whole within.

cone_outer.doc: The angle, in degrees, beyond which it is heard at cone_outer_gain.

record.doc: Where a voice or sound is, as a PannerNode places it: from the listener, equal-power panned by its azimuth (in place of its pan), and quieted by its distance model and its cone. Positions and orientations glide as gains do (AUDIO_GLIDE_MS); the rest change at once. A voice that gains or loses its panner starts afresh, as one whose bus changed; a panner that places nothing is ignored, and of two for one voice or sound hosts take the first.

max.doc: The most panners one frame may declare: one for each voice and sound it may have.

extensions.doc: The game's own sections, which its pen.json `protocol` declares, after the rest of the packet: a marker, their count, then each one's tag, length and values. A packet without any ends before the marker. Tag 0 is reserved for one optional development provenance block: at most MAX_PROVENANCE_LANES UTF-8 JSON bytes as float32 lanes, version 1 with entries of first/end packet lane ranges and optional object, system, source (file/start/end UTF-8 byte span). See docs/packet-diagnostics.md. Hosts consume this metadata without retaining it in the rendered frame; release games omit it.

max.doc: The most of a game's own sections one frame may carry.

tag.doc: A game's own sections and events are numbered from 1 to this.

lanes.doc: The most lanes one of a game's own sections may carry.
